projects.title: Tensor-Core-Optimized Fused Attention Kernel Suite
projects.summary: Build a custom fused attention kernel (Triton/CUDA) optimized for tensor cores, extend it with FP8/INT8 quantization, wrap it as a PyTorch custom op, and use the resulting memory/throughput headroom to run a longer context length or larger batch than the unoptimized baseline could support on the same GPU. This demonstrates the low-level kernel craft, precision/memory-bandwidth engineering, and stack-spanning integration the role calls out, plus the direct link between an infra optimization and a new model capability.

components.name: Fused tensor-core attention kernel
components.description: Implement a flash-attention-style fused kernel in Triton or raw CUDA that explicitly targets tensor core execution paths, then profile it with Nsight Compute against a naive PyTorch attention implementation to quantify occupancy and SM utilization gains.
components.rationale: A working kernel with measured utilization/occupancy improvements over a naive baseline is direct, reproducible evidence of tensor-core-level kernel optimization skill and its effect on utilization.

components.name: Mixed-precision / FP8-INT8 variant
components.description: Extend the kernel with FP8 and INT8 quantized code paths, measuring memory bandwidth usage and end-to-end throughput/latency versus the FP16/BF16 baseline at matched accuracy tolerance.
components.rationale: Quantifying throughput and bandwidth gains from a self-built low-precision kernel path is concrete evidence of the quantization and memory-bandwidth expertise the listing seeks, and of inference-efficiency improvement.

components.name: PyTorch custom-op integration
components.description: Register the kernel as a custom PyTorch operator (with autograd/inference support as applicable) and swap it into a small transformer model end to end, verifying correctness and compatibility with torch.compile.
components.rationale: Carrying an optimization from raw CUDA/Triton up through operator registration into a real model shows the hardware-to-framework range the role explicitly requires.

components.name: Capability-unlock benchmark
components.description: Use the memory savings from the quantized kernel to run a strictly longer context length or larger batch on identical hardware than the unoptimized model could fit without OOM, and report the throughput/latency delta.
components.rationale: Showing a concrete case where a kernel-level optimization is the enabling factor for a capability (longer context) that was otherwise infeasible directly mirrors the claim that infra work enables new model capabilities.

roadmap.milestone: Working fused tensor-core kernel with Nsight-verified utilization gains over baseline
FP8/INT8 quantized kernel variant with measured bandwidth and throughput improvements
Kernel wrapped as a PyTorch custom op inside a runnable transformer model
Demonstrated longer-context/larger-batch capability unlock with before/after benchmarks

projects.title: Small-Scale Multi-GPU Orchestration & Fault-Tolerant Training
projects.summary: Stand up a multi-GPU (e.g., 4-8 GPU) distributed training pipeline using tensor/pipeline parallelism over NCCL, build a lightweight orchestration/synchronization layer with live utilization monitoring, and inject simulated node failures to prove checkpoint-based recovery. This project is scaled down from 'thousands of GPUs' but demonstrates the same coordination, communication-overhead, and fault-tolerance principles the role is hired to solve at scale.

components.name: Model-parallel NCCL training pipeline
components.description: Implement tensor and/or pipeline parallelism across several GPUs using NCCL collectives directly, then profile and optimize the overlap of compute with communication to reduce collective-communication overhead.
components.rationale: Directly building and tuning a model-parallel pipeline on real NCCL collectives is hands-on evidence of reducing communication overhead and coordinating multiple GPUs, the same primitives used at thousands-of-GPU scale.

components.name: Synchronization/orchestration harness with utilization dashboard
components.description: Build a lightweight coordinator that manages barriers, rank assignment, and elastic worker changes across the GPU pool, alongside a real-time dashboard showing per-GPU utilization during scale-out and scale-in events.
components.rationale: A self-built orchestration layer plus utilization telemetry is direct evidence of understanding the coordination problem and of keeping GPUs busy during synchronization events, the core skill named for cluster-scale orchestration.

components.name: Fault injection and checkpoint/resume
components.description: Simulate worker crashes mid-training and demonstrate automatic checkpoint-based recovery, measuring how much compute is lost versus a run with no fault tolerance in place.
components.rationale: A measured before/after comparison of wasted compute with and without checkpoint/resume is concrete evidence of building fault tolerance into training infrastructure.

components.name: Framework-integrated distributed config
components.description: Combine the raw-NCCL orchestration logic with PyTorch DDP/FSDP configuration in the same pipeline, showing the custom low-level primitives and the higher-level framework working together.
components.rationale: Interleaving hand-written NCCL orchestration with standard framework-level distributed training shows the same hardware-to-framework range as the kernel project but from the distributed-systems side.

roadmap.milestone: Multi-GPU tensor/pipeline-parallel training running over NCCL with measured communication overhead
Orchestration harness with live utilization dashboard across scale events
Fault-injection tests showing checkpoint/resume compute-loss reduction
Unified pipeline combining custom NCCL orchestration with DDP/FSDP

projects.title: Self-Directed Inference Performance Investigation
projects.summary: Pick an existing open-source inference stack, profile it end to end without a predefined ticket, independently identify and fix the biggest bottleneck, and write it up as an internal-RFC-style report. This project is the weakest on raw kernel/systems depth of the three but is the most direct demonstration of operating in an ambiguous, undefined problem space and communicating impact-driven results, which the other two projects don't showcase.

components.name: Open-ended profiling investigation
components.description: Choose an open-source LLM inference server (e.g., vLLM or llama.cpp), profile GPU utilization and latency end to end with no predefined target, and document the hypothesis-driven process of narrowing down to the single biggest bottleneck.
components.rationale: Self-scoping an investigation from scratch with no ticket or spec is direct evidence of defining one's own path forward in an ambiguous problem space, applied to a real utilization bottleneck.

components.name: Targeted fix and validation
components.description: Implement a fix for the identified bottleneck (e.g., a scheduler change, KV-cache layout change, or kernel fusion) and measure the before/after latency and throughput impact under a realistic workload.
components.rationale: Delivering a measurable inference-efficiency improvement that the applicant chose and scoped themselves is evidence of both inference-efficiency skill and independent judgment under ambiguity.

components.name: RFC-style performance report
components.description: Write a short internal-RFC-style document covering the problem statement, alternatives considered, measured impact, and recommended follow-on work, in the style used to communicate infrastructure decisions to a research/engineering team.
components.rationale: A clear written artifact showing how ambiguous problems were scoped, prioritized, and communicated is evidence tailored specifically to the 'define your own path forward' requirement, beyond what code alone shows.

roadmap.milestone: Documented end-to-end profiling investigation identifying the primary bottleneck
Implemented fix with before/after throughput and latency measurements
Published RFC-style write-up of the investigation and recommendations
